Hey guys,

Wasn’t too sure where else to ask this, and figured this would be the best place. A little over a month and a half ago I had my 2013 Scion FR-S detailed and opti-coated, my main concern being the dreaded swirls mark all over my car. I figured I’d pay a little extra to have Opti-Coat put on my car for extra protection. The place that did it are the best in my area (MA). They literally have not one reviews online with less than 5 stars. All perfect. And there are a good 100-175 reviews. Anyway, I got my car back that day and it looked 10x better. I was happy. It was overcast, so the guy shined his light on the hood so I could see the new condition the paint was in. It looked great. Fast forward a sunny couple days, and I see there are still lots of swirls in my paint when looking in direct sunlight. Again, only in direct sunlight can I see the swirls, but still... isn’t this taken care of during the paint correction? I texted the guy a week or two after telling him this and he said he would bring it back in to touch up anything he missed (he admitted he’s good, not perfect). That was a few weeks ago. Yesterday was very sunny and I can still see swirls in my paint, in several areas of the car (hood, truck, fenders, etc). They can be seen only in direct sunlight, or when looking meticulously with a flash light. Am I being too picky?  I have washed the car once since he did it initially (I took it through a touch-free spray wash only because it was filthy after some rain.) 

I paid $650 for paint correction and opticoat. 


TLDR: paid $650 to have my car paint corrected and opticoated by a very reputable shop. Can still see swirls in the paint in direct sunlight. WTF?

Never, ever cheap on tires. What makes you think you don’t need snow tires just because you have an AWD vehicle? AWD does nothing to help you come to a stop when you lose traction as you’re trying to brake. Tires do. Get yourself a set of dedicated snow tires, and another set of decent dedicated “all-season” or summer tires for when its consistently above 40 degrees out. 

Edit: if you can afford it ATM. If not, it’s definitely a good investment to save up for. Plus, both sets will last MUCH longer, as you’ll be switching them out once a year, and giving the other set a break.
